claims.statement: Capex expected to continue at INR 300-600 crore per year
Growth in FY25 expected similar to FY24 with Q1 slow due to elections
EBITDA margin improvement expected to continue
EGT localization line SOP April 2025 at Bosch plant
Capex estimated at INR 400-600 crore for localization goals over next 3-5 years
CV injector assembly line in Nashik ramped up; third-party supplier localization ongoing
Building Technologies secured pivotal projects across metros, airports, government, energy, consumer, education, health sectors
Building Technologies divestiture expected to close by Q1-Q2 2025
EBITDA margin improved to 13.2% in Q4 FY24 from 12.9% in Q4 FY23
FY24 EBITDA margin improved to 12.5% from 12.1% in FY23
Other expenses reduced to 14.7% in March 2024 from 16.8% in March 2023 due to cost measures and divestment
Production line (2nd) inauguration for Lambda Sensors (LSFmh) at Bosch Bidadi plant to support BS6 ODBII stage B regulation effective April 2025
Management maintains broad expectation of moderate growth for FY25 similar to FY24 despite election year dynamics and high base effects.
EBITDA margin improved to 12% in Q1 FY25 from 11.3% in Q1 FY24 due to revenue growth and reduction in other expenses.
Management aims to maintain double-digit EBITDA margin but will not provide future margin guidance due to technology transition uncertainties.
Capex will be spent for feasible and profitable localization; no fixed range but investments made when they contribute to top and bottom line.
NOx sensor line investment includes export volumes to achieve better utilization and return on investment.
Second Lambda sensor production line inaugurated at Bidadi plant in April 2024; targeting over 8 million pieces annually by 2025.
Power Tools India elevated to independent region covering SAARC countries effective April 1, 2024; exports from Chennai plant to serve region.
Indian economy growth forecast 7.0% in FY2024-25 per IMF July 2024
Global economy growth forecast 3.2% in 2024 per IMF July 2024
Indian automotive market expected to grow annually 3%-4% long term
Q2 FY25 EBITDA grew 14.1% YoY to INR 5,605 million; EBITDA margin improved from 11.9% to 12.8% due to revenue growth and material cost improvement
H1 FY25 EBITDA grew 12.6% YoY to INR 10,802 million; EBITDA margin improved from 11.6% to 12.4% due to revenue growth and material cost improvement
Full year FY25 capex guided at roughly INR 4,000 million, lower than last year as Adugodi campus finished; mainly plant and machinery
Equipped to handle pre-buy volumes before TREM V; work closely with OEMs to support capacity increases as done in past norm transitions
FY25 growth indicators suggest mirroring 2024 growth rates; constantly evaluate and adapt business plan at regular intervals
Management expects aftermarket business growth of 8% to 10% in FY26.
Steady-state employee cost targeted at 8% to 10% of revenue depending on product mix.
Building Technologies division divested with EBIT margin of about 6%.
Gross margin improvement driven by product mix, carryover of RMI and ECI from big customers, and material cost reduction measures.
Consumer goods margin decline is seasonal; expect recovery in other quarters.
Global R&D investment consistently 6% to 8% of sales; over €2.5bn in fuel cells and €7-8bn in electrification over 10-15 years.
LSFmh ramp-up at Bidadi plant progressing for OBD2 implementation with OEMs by April 2025.
NOx line inauguration in Bidadi Plant
Expects to grow beyond industry growth rates driven by premiumization, new regulations, technology trends, and electrification breakthroughs
Inaugurated NOx sensor Gen-3 line at Bidadi plant in 67 days; scaling to 2.1 million sensors per year by 2027
No new orders received for electric two-wheelers; current order book continues as is
EBITDA margin improved from 12.5% to 12.8% in FY25 driven by revenue growth, material cost reduction, and expense control
NOx sensor Gen-3 line capacity scaling to 2.1 million sensors per year by 2027
Revenue from operations in Q1 FY26 was INR 47,886 million, up 10.9% YoY; EBITDA was INR 6,393 million, up 23% YoY on revenue growth and material cost improvement.
EBITDA margin improved YoY due to revenue growth and material cost improvement; PAT margin rose to 23.3% from 10.8% YoY due to improved EBITDA and profit on sale of building technologies businesses.
Two-wheeler volumes will stabilize after ramp-up; 40% QoQ growth due to new projects.
Localization continuously increasing; on track with intent to increase localization content; decisions factor geopolitics, tariffs, and export volumes.
EBITDA grew 10.1% YoY to INR 6,171 million in Q2 FY26 with margin improvement from favorable product mix and expense optimization
Material cost progress from favorable product mix and localization strategy
Well prepared with capacity for increased ABS demand if two-wheeler ABS mandate implemented as per draft
Expect 8-15% hydrogen ICE market penetration in heavy commercial vehicles by around 2030
Expects PV, Tractors, 2W to hit all-time high production in FY26; LCV sub-segment also to reach all-time high
EBITDA grew 5.1% YoY to INR6,124 million in Q3 FY26; margin improvement driven by favorable product mix and expense optimization
Q3 FY26 EBIT margin at 10.5% after first provision for New Labour Code
Capex for FY27-28 under consideration; no guidance given; investments adjusted based on customer volume forecasts and capacity utilization buffers
Bidadi plant awarded CII SCALE Awards 2025 for digital excellence and innovation in logistics; integrated autonomous digital ecosystem automates entire logistics value stream

Margin improvement trajectory: last 3 years show PAT growth from cost improvement and localization; product mix and new product localization cycles temper near-term margin expansion; no 3-4 year guidance given
Expect market momentum to continue in coming quarter and better performance going forward
Indian automotive market outlook for 2026-27 remains in the growth trajectory with expectation of high single-digit growth
Indian power tools market expected to grow at CAGR of around ~7% over next 3 years
Acquisition of RBIC expected to be completed by end of Q1 2026-27
Capital Expenditure (excluding capital advance, capital creditors and ROU) Rs 214.5 crore
Proforma FY25 EPS accretion: Bosch Ltd standalone 683, combined with RBIC 720
Expected pro forma EPS accretion of approximately 5% based on FY25 numbers
RBIC order book very full with strong project pipeline for next four to five years
RBIC EBITDA margin expanded from 12.8% to 19.3% over FY23-25; margins seen as stable going forward
Capex managed via modular product platforms and relocation of idle lines from global network; capex at reasonable percentage of total net sales
Three state-of-the-art facilities in Chakan, Manesar, Sanand; in-house manufacturing for majority portfolio gives control over quality, lead times, cost
FY2027 production outlook: PV Low 5.61M High 5.90M
FY2027 production outlook: CV Low 0.71M High 0.73M
FY2027 production outlook: 3W Low 0.48M High 0.48M
FY2027 production outlook: 2W Low 26.86M High 28.27M
FY27 outlook is cautiously optimistic with flattish volume growth expected across segments due to geopolitical headwinds
EBITDA margin improved in Q4 FY26 and FY26 due to revenue growth, material cost reduction and expense control
Power Solutions division surpassed INR 130 billion total net sales for calendar year 2025
Joint venture with Brakes India and Wheels India aims to commence operations by end of 2026
Two-Wheeler division maintained 100% delivery commitment to all OEMs with zero production disruptions
Revenue from operations in Q1 FY27 stood at INR58,419 million, up 22% YoY and 5% QoQ
EBITDA in Q1 FY27 was INR8,180 million, up 28% YoY and 4.7% QoQ; margin improvement driven by revenue growth and expense optimization
Profit after tax declined 37.1% YoY due to exceptional item in prior year; excluding exceptional item, PAT grew 9.9% YoY and 23.4% QoQ
Management confident of sustaining EBITDA margins above 14% driven by operational excellence, localization, volume growth, productivity and favorable product mix
Growth drivers for next 3-5 years: volume growth across mobility portfolio, new product introductions, new technology introductions (CV ADAS), premiumization and volume increase in vehicles
Expects modest second half FY27 due to high base, inflation, weak monsoon, and rate tightening
Expects flat to modest growth in Q3 FY27 relative to high prior-year base
RBIC EBITDA margin declined due to raw material prices, forex, depreciation change, and capacity investments; expects recovery in subsequent quarters
Bosch Limited margins on upward track despite transient forex and raw material impacts; endeavor to maintain and improve margins
H1 FY27 capex INR350 crores; annual spend focused on upgrading production lines for volume output
RBIC Chakan plant surpassed 20 million active safety units cumulative across ESP, ABS, and two-wheeler ABS platforms
Chennai power tools plant surpassed 20 million power tools production milestone
RBIC commissioning additional line for ABS10M two-wheeler ABS capacity increase and new-generation ESP10 start of production
